headline: ماذا حدث حين حاولت المستشفيات منع مقاطعة الممرضين في أثناء إعطاء الأدوية؟
reviewer: AI editorial review using the owner's arabic-editorial-reviewer and english-editorial-reviewer agents (not a human reader test)

introduction_answers.problem: يُقاطَع الممرضون كثيرًا في أثناء جولة الأدوية، وترتبط المقاطعة بأخطاء أكثر في أغلب الدراسات.
introduction_answers.change: جرّبت مستشفيات سترة «لا تقاطعني»، فلم تجد تجربة وُزّعت فيها الوحدات بالقرعة أنها خفّضت الأخطاء.

summary: جرّبت مستشفيات فرنسية سترة «لا تقاطعني» لتقليل أخطاء إعطاء الدواء، فلم تجد تجربة عشوائية أثرًا لها، وتشير الدراسات إلى أن مصادر المقاطعة أوسع مما تمنعه سترة.
terminology_evidence: Interruption, medication administration error, opportunity for error, randomized and cluster randomized trial, systematic review and scoping review are explained at first use or in the glossary; English terms are in parentheses after the Arabic.
language_evidence: Reviewed by the arabic-editorial-reviewer agent (two BLOCK rounds fixed) and the english-editorial-reviewer agent (BLOCK on 'precise work' calque fixed); editorial simulation, not a human reader test.

mobile_evidence.scope: Automated rendered-layout verification; screenshots retained for human visual review

source_evidence.claim: 22 quantitative studies in 9 countries; 16 (73%) significant positive association between interruptions and medication administration errors; definitions varied
source_evidence.assessment: Scoping review (Schroers et al., J Adv Nurs 2025)

source_evidence.claim: 1,000-bed teaching hospital, Saudi Arabia; 28 nurses, 15 medication rounds; 182 interruptions; frequent sources nurses, doctors and impediments
source_evidence.assessment: Small descriptive observational and interview study (Eid et al., 2022)

source_evidence.claim: 51 studies; pharmacists interrupted from fewer than 5 to more than 20 times per hour; phone calls, customer questions, staff questions outside their scope

29 units, 4 French hospitals, 178 nurses, 1,346 patients, 383 rounds; error rate 7.09% vs 6.23% of opportunities for error (p=0.192); interruption rate = doses with at least one interruption / all doses: pre 13.4% vs 23.78%, during 15.04% vs 20.75%; authors: no impact on errors or interruption rates; main error wrong dosage form; most errors no clinical impact
source_evidence.location: Abstract and Results (full text PMC8383384, Table 3)
source_evidence.assessment: Cluster randomized controlled trial, data collected March-July 2017

source_evidence.claim: 14 studies; preventive strategies may reduce external interruptions, nurse-to-nurse interruptions remained common; responsive strategies improved handling; effect on errors inconclusive
source_evidence.assessment: Systematic review without meta-analysis (Zhang et al., 2025)

decision: CI candidate PASS only; authoritative approval is successful GitHub Actions job
